press.why:
Skin-care ingredient labels are long, technical, and unforgiving — and when a child breaks out, you usually have no way to know which ingredient caused it. Skinllergic Cam scans a label in one shot, flags risky ingredients per family member, and adds a "compare allergic products" feature: line up every product that gave a reaction and surface the ingredient that keeps reappearing — that's the real allergen. All ingredient matching and AI inference run on-device; personal allergen data never leaves your phone.

v2.0 adds iCloud cross-device sync, multi-family mode (parents tracking allergens for babies and older relatives without their own phones), Home Screen and Lock Screen Widgets, monthly seasonal reminders, iOS Shortcuts, and OCR for Japanese / Korean labels. Built by a solo iOS developer in Taiwan using the latest Apple technologies — small, focused, and quietly thoughtful.
press.founder:
I have three daughters, each with different skin sensitivities. Whenever they broke out, I had no way to tell which ingredient was the culprit — I'd just switch brands, watch the rash come back, and guess again.

Skinllergic Cam is built around that frustration. Beyond scanning a single product, the heart of the app is the "compare allergic products" feature: line up every product that gave one of my kids a reaction, find the ingredient that keeps showing up — that's the real allergen.

Later I added multi-family mode (so each daughter has her own list), Apple Intelligence to explain ingredients in plain language, and iCloud sync so allergen info stays in step across devices. As a solo iOS developer, I wanted to use the latest Apple technologies to make something genuinely useful for my own kids — and share it with every family in the same boat.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Skinllergic Cam is built around a simple principle: your allergen data is yours. This policy explains, in plain language, what data the app handles, where it lives, and what we (the developer) can or cannot see.
tldr: Ingredient recognition (OCR) runs on your device. Photos and ingredient text never leave the device.
AI ingredient explanations use Apple Intelligence on-device. No cloud AI is involved.
Your personal allergen profile (family members, allergens, scanned products, scan history) is stored in your private iCloud container — encrypted by Apple. The developer cannot read it.
Sign in uses Sign in with Apple. We never see your name, email, or Apple ID.
No third-party analytics, no ad SDKs, no trackers.
Vendor product data (used by the optional recommendations feature) is stored on Supabase and is not linked to your personal profile.
privacy.section1:
On-device only: photos you take to scan ingredients, recognized text from those photos, AI-generated ingredient explanations, OCR language preferences. None of this is uploaded to any server — including ours.

iCloud private container: family member profiles, allergen list, saved products, scan history, app settings. This data syncs across your own Apple devices through Apple's CloudKit infrastructure. Apple holds the encryption keys; we have no access.

Vendor data (separate): the optional recommendations feature reads a public catalog of skincare products from Supabase. It does not write anything about you to that catalog.
privacy.section2: We use Sign in with Apple as the sole sign-in method. Apple does not share your email or name with us unless you explicitly choose to. The app only sees an opaque user identifier used for routing iCloud data.
privacy.section3:
We cannot see your scanned photos, recognized ingredients, family member names, allergens, products, or scan history. All of these live either on your device or in your iCloud private container.

We can see aggregate App Store metrics (downloads, country, version) provided by Apple to all developers. These are not linked to individual users.
privacy.section4:
Supabase: stores the public vendor product catalog used by the recommendations feature. No personal data is sent to Supabase.
Apple iCloud / CloudKit: stores your personal allergen data in a private container encrypted by Apple.
Apple Sign In: handles authentication.

There are no other third-party services. No Google Analytics, no Firebase, no Crashlytics, no Sentry, no Facebook SDK, no advertising SDKs.
privacy.section5: Skinllergic Cam is designed to help parents track allergens for their children. The parent operates the app on their own device with their own Apple ID; the child does not interact with the app directly. We do not knowingly collect data from children under 13.
privacy.section6: You can delete all of your data at any time by signing out and removing the app, or by signing out and deleting your iCloud data for the app via Settings → Apple ID → iCloud → Manage Account Storage.
privacy.section7: If we make material changes, we will update the "Last updated" date and, where appropriate, notify you within the app.
privacy.section8: Questions? Email ccccaiwork@gmail.com. We typically reply within 24 hours, in English or Traditional Chinese.

faq.q: Does Skinllergic Cam send my data to the cloud?
faq.a: Your personal allergen profile syncs across your own Apple devices via iCloud (encrypted by Apple). The developer cannot read it. Ingredient OCR and AI explanations run entirely on-device. See the Privacy Policy for details.

faq.q: Why isn't Apple Intelligence showing the AI explanations?
faq.a: Apple Intelligence requires iOS 26+ on a supported device (iPhone 15 Pro or later). If you're on an older device or older iOS, the rest of the app works normally — only the AI plain-language explanations are unavailable.

faq.q: I deleted the app and reinstalled. Will my allergens come back?
faq.a: Yes. Sign in with the same Apple ID and your iCloud-synced data (family members, allergens, products, scans) will restore automatically.

faq.q: I switched to a new iPhone. Will my data follow?
faq.a: Yes. Sign in with Apple on the new device and iCloud will sync everything within a few minutes.

faq.q: Which languages does the OCR support?
faq.a: English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. You can pick which languages to enable in Settings → OCR Languages.

faq.q: How many family members can I add?
faq.a: Up to five — typically enough for a household. The "me" profile is created automatically.

faq.q: Can I export my allergen list?
faq.a: Allergen lists can be exported and imported through the Allergen List tab. Useful for sharing with doctors or backing up before changes.

faq.q: Is the app really free? What's the catch?
faq.a: Yes, free. No in-app purchases, no ads, no third-party trackers. The app is built and maintained by a solo developer who wanted a tool that worked for his own kids.

faq.q: I found a wrong ingredient match / bug — how do I report it?
faq.a: Email ccccaiwork@gmail.com with a screenshot or short description. Specific is better — "product X says ingredient Y is risky but Y is the salt form, not the parent compound" is more helpful than "the matching is wrong".
Yes — email is best. The roadmap is set by what feels useful for families with sensitive skin, so anecdotes about your situation help calibrate priorities.
